title: Dynamic Stabilisation

positions.as_written: Examine muscle bulk and control as part of assessing medial stability.
Expect a graft harvest from gracilis and semitendinosus to alter dynamic medial restraint, which is anatomy rather than a complication.
Protect the saphenous nerve where it emerges between sartorius and gracilis, because the interval used for harvest is the interval the nerve uses.
Consider separate innervation when a single pes tendon is weak.
Treat medial stability as the sum of a static limit and a dynamic tension, and state which one a finding refers to.
Consider graft source when the medial side is already injured, because the pes is both a graft and a stabiliser.
Assess dynamic restraint under anaesthetic and awake, and record the difference.
Protect the saphenous nerve by finding it rather than by avoiding its territory.
Avoid attributing medial laxity to ligament alone in a wasted limb.
